articles.title: Severe penalties following the shameful brawl in the Spain-Argentina World Cup final
articles.standfirst: 10 matches for Paredes... and one for Gavi
articles.summary: 10 matches for Paredes... and one for Gavi
articles.body:
The FIFA has already issued its sanctions, a month later, after the shameful brawl following the World Cup final between Argentina and Spain. And there’s something for everyone.

It will be a 1 0-match suspension for Leandro Paredes , the wildest of all in that final stretch, seven for Nahuel Molina , who hit Rodri for no reason, another for Almada , who held Gavi while Leandro was hitting him, three for Ayala , who threw a punch at Dani Olmo , and another for Gavi , the only one given to a Spanish player, after shoving Eric García , who also got a warning from Paredes.

It has been the Disciplinary Committee of the highest governing body in world football that has sanctioned these four members of the Argentine delegation, also including heavy financial penalties.

Specifically with 77,000 euros for Paredes and Molina ($90,000), and 25,000 euros ( $33,000) for Almada, Ayala (a member of the coaching staff and former footballer) and for the Barcelona player.

articles.title: FIFA harshly punishes Argentina after the controversial Falkland Islands flag
articles.standfirst: The highest governing body of international football imposes a financial and disciplinary sanction on the AFA over the banner about the sovereignty of the Malvinas Islands displayed after the World Cup semifinals
articles.summary: The highest governing body of international football imposes a financial and disciplinary sanction on the AFA over the banner about the sovereignty of the Malvinas Islands displayed after the World Cup semifinals
articles.body:
The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has issued a forceful ruling that shakes the foundations of South American football . After weeks of deliberation following the conclusion of the 2026 World Cup , the Zurich-based body formalized disciplinary proceedings against the Argentine Football Association (AFA) for directly violating the Disciplinary Code regarding neutrality and geopolitics.

The main focus of the penalty falls on the display of the banner bearing the slogan "The Falkland Islands are Argentine" , unfurled by the Albiceleste players on the pitch. The incident, which occurred after the victory over the England national team in the semifinals of the intercontinental tournament , was classified by the governing body's inspectors as a clear violation of the regulations.

The violation of Article 13 and FIFA's geopolitical veto

In its official statement, the highest governing body of world football bases the fine on the violation of Article 13 , section 2 c) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (FDC) . Said section categorically prohibits the use of official sporting events to carry out demonstrations or proclamations of a nature unrelated to the practice of football.

Sources consulted by Argentine media outlets such as Página/12 and Infobae confirmed that the direct financial sanction linked exclusively to the flag amounts to 10,000 U.S. dollars . Additional fines are added to this amount for inappropriate conduct and lack of order in the stadiums , raising the package of financial penalties to significantly higher figures.

Attendance restrictions for upcoming official matches

In addition to the economic impact on the AFA's coffers, the ruling imposes a severe sporting punishment for Argentina's upcoming home matches . FIFA ordered that the national team play its next two official matches on Argentine soil with a 50% crowd capacity restriction.

However, the body opened the possibility of a conditional suspension for part of the punishment . Under a probationary period established by the Disciplinary Committee, half of the attendance restriction and a portion of the fines will be suspended depending on the conduct of the delegation and of Argentine fans during the upcoming international dates .

The FA background and British protests

The display of the flag did not go unnoticed at the time by the English Football Association (FA), which lodged a formal complaint with FIFA delegates immediately after the semifinal match. The British complaint demanded exemplary measures considering the historical sensitivity of the territorial dispute over the South Atlantic archipelago .

Although in England there was initially speculation about harsh sporting suspensions for the footballers who held up the banner on the field of play, the disciplinary tribunal chose to apply the standard regulations regarding political slogans . In this way, the administrative responsibility fell entirely on the national federation.

The AFA's historical stance regarding diplomatic claims

It is not the first time that the AFA has faced disciplinary proceedings over the Malvinas issue. Similar precedents in friendly matches and previous qualifiers had already been the subject of warnings from FIFA and CONMEBOL , bodies that maintain a strict "zero tolerance" policy toward sovereign or political claims within the framework of the game.

Despite repeated warnings from the governing bodies, the cause of the Malvinas Islands remains deeply tied to the cultural identity of Argentine football . The players' stance at the World Cup reflected a deeply rooted sentiment that has historically clashed with the neutrality rules required by FIFA statutes for tournaments of global scope.

A ruling that sets a precedent for future competitions

Various analysts and international sports experts agree that the ratification of this sanction seeks to set a firm precedent ahead of upcoming international competitions. FIFA seeks to prevent stadiums from becoming platforms for geopolitical disputes between participating nations.

National media outlets such as TN and TyC Sports highlighted that the ruling not only affects the financial sphere, but imposes the obligation to allocate a sum of $100,000 to anti-discrimination programs and awareness initiatives in stadiums , as part of the comprehensive package of corrective measures.

The steps to be followed by the AFA leadership

Following the official notification at the headquarters on Viamonte Street, the AFA's legal team has a period of ten days to request the full grounds of the ruling . The Argentine leadership is analyzing whether it will file an appeal before FIFA's Appeal Committee in an attempt to reduce the fines and lift the partial closure of the stadium.

The outcome of this case marks a milestone in the relationship between FIFA regulations and expressions of patriotic content in South America, reopening the controversy over how far the national teams' freedom of expression extends on the biggest stage in world sport .

articles.title: Gianni Infantino at odds with FIFA itself and is defying its vice president
articles.standfirst: The president’s Caribbean appearance came amid mounting pressure over failed investment proposal
articles.summary: The president’s Caribbean appearance came amid mounting pressure over failed investment proposal
articles.body:
A youth soccer tournament in Punta Cana became the latest stage for FIFA’s escalating internal power struggle after Gianni Infantino chose to attend despite a direct request from one of the organization’s own vice presidents to stay away.

Victor Montagliani , the CONCACAF president and a FIFA vice president, had warned that Infantino ’s appearance at the Caribbean Football Union Under-14 Series risked turning attention away from the players and toward the controversy surrounding FIFA’s leadership.

Infantino went anyway. He appeared at the event Saturday and shared images of meetings with Dominican officials, including Sports and Recreation Minister Kelvin Cruz and Dominican Football Federation president Jose Deschamps , making clear he had no intention of retreating from the public stage.

The decision came during one of the most turbulent periods of Infantino ’s 11-year presidency, with powerful officials from Europe, Asia and North America increasingly challenging his authority.

“I believe that considering the governance crisis surrounding FIFA as a result of your controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, the media will focus on this situation,” Montagliani wrote in an open letter, as per The Associated Press.

He added: “As such, I respectfully ask you in the name of football to reconsider your attendance as it will unfortunately undermine the technical nature of this important youth development activity.”

Growing resistance inside world soccer

The dispute centers on the collapse of the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, a plan that would have shifted FIFA’s multi-billion-dollar commercial operations into a subsidiary partly owned by outside investors.

The proposed structure would have given investors led by Joshua Kushner a 20 percent stake, prompting fierce criticism once the plan became public.

Infantino withdrew the project on August 1 after a wave of opposition from soccer officials and supporters. The backlash intensified further when FIFA chief operating officer Kevin Lamour publicly criticized both the proposal and Infantino’s leadership style. Lamour was fired this week.

Montagliani has since aligned himself with UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin and Asian Football Confederation president Sheik Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa , turning what had been private concern into an increasingly open confrontation.

Caribbean associations could now become politically significant, particularly if Infantino looks to build support outside CONCACAF’s leadership structure.

Re-election fight adds another layer to FIFA rift

The timing of the dispute matters. Infantino is seeking a fourth and final term as FIFA president, which would keep him in office through 2031.

The election is scheduled to take place at next year’s FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco, with potential challengers required to enter the race by November 18.

He has also largely avoided substantive public questioning since the investment plan became public.

When Sky News reporter James Matthews approached him in Punta Cana and asked whether he had betrayed the sport and should resign, Infantino replied, “Thank you so much,” before making jokes about both men being bald.

That exchange only added to the sense that FIFA’s leadership battle is moving beyond policy disagreements and into a broader test of authority.

A visit to an Under-14 tournament would ordinarily have attracted little international attention. Instead, by rejecting Montagliani ’s request, Infantino turned it into another visible sign that he intends to stand his ground as opposition inside world soccer continues to grow.

articles.title: The UEFA lifts the boycott of FIFA competitions, but goes all in for Gianni Infantino's departure
articles.standfirst: The European body will reverse the suspension of its national teams after halting the sale of the World Cup to private capital
articles.summary: The European body will reverse the suspension of its national teams after halting the sale of the World Cup to private capital
articles.body:
'World football breathes a sigh of relief on the pitch, but is preparing for a real all-out battle in the political offices . In a high-impact strategic move, UEFA will make official before its 55 member federations the end of the boycott it had maintained against FIFA competitions . The decision allows the teams representing the "Old Continent" to compete normally again on the international calendar , unlocking an unprecedented crisis that threatened to bring global tournaments to a halt .'

This sporting truce comes after intense behind-the-scenes negotiations in which the European body managed to freeze the controversial privatization project of the tournaments organized by football’s governing body. With the confirmation that there will be no transfer of assets to private investors, the UEFA national teams will immediately resume their international commitments, marking the end of the competitive standstill.

The condition UEFA set to unlock the conflict

According to information revealed by the British newspaper The Times, the leaders of European football's governing body will formally announce the measure during the executives' summit to be held this Thursday in Monaco . To reach this point, the European leadership demanded strict compliance with two non-negotiable premises: the definitive cancellation of the plan to sell private stakes and the formal guarantee that a similar initiative will never be presented again.

The conflict reached its turning point in late July, when FIFA capitulated and withdrew the FIFA Forward Enterprises (FFE) project proposal in the face of unanimous rejection from clubs, players, and fans . With the contractual assurance that control of the World Cup and its satellite tournaments will not be subject to commercial distortions, UEFA has given the green light for teams such as England's women's Under-20 national team to travel to their official fixtures without any restrictions.

Legal siege and call for the resignation of Gianni Infantino

However, lifting the boycott does not mean a peace flag for FIFA president Gianni Infantino . According to reports by the EFE agency and international outlets such as TN and López-Dóriga Digital, the leadership headed by Aleksander Čeferin has decided to separate sporting participation from political persecution, now focusing all its institutional firepower on forcing the Swiss leader's resignation.

From the headquarters in Nyon, the firm position is maintained that Infantino crossed a red line by trying to commercialize the historic assets of international football . UEFA maintains that the president has lost the support not only political of the voters, but that of the entire global football community , including coaches, footballers, and fans who strongly opposed the privatization of the flagship tournament.

A multimillion-dollar lawsuit in U.S. courts

To increase the pressure on Infantino, the European body's legal services hired law firms in the United States to send a formal warning to the leadership in Zurich. In that legal notice, UEFA warns of the imminent initiation of arbitration claims, regulatory actions and lawsuits for alleged mismanagement in the development of the FFE corporate structure .

The legal document imposes on FIFA and 14 of its top executives the immediate obligation to identify, preserve, and not alter any document, email, or electronic file linked to the private project . This prearranged measure marks the first procedural step toward a multimillion-dollar lawsuit in the American courts, with the clear intention of cornering the president's management.

Heading toward the elections and candidates in the shadows

On the political front, UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin has reiterated that Infantino should step aside before the next elections of the governing body scheduled for March . Should the current leader insist on seeking reelection, the European bloc and its allies intend to put forward a strong alternative candidacy capable of unseating the Italian-Swiss executive.

Although Čeferin ruled out leading FIFA's presidential ticket himself to avoid conflicts of interest, in the corridors of the European federations, strategic alliances are already being woven to put forward a consensus candidate who guarantees transparent governance and remains far removed from private investment funds.

The future of global football after the storm

With the confirmation of the lifting of operational restrictions, the structure of international football regains a certain normality on the pitch . Fans will once again be able to enjoy the qualifiers and world tournaments without the fear of massive absences from the European powerhouses .

However, the political front promises months of high tension and uncertainty in the sports leadership . The battle between Nyon and Zurich has gone from a strike on the pitch to a direct clash in the courts, where Gianni Infantino's stay at the head of world football will depend on his ability to withstand the offensive of the most powerful confederation on the planet .

articles.title: FIFA changes the sanctions against Argentina's players after the World Cup final
articles.standfirst: Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina, and Thiago Almada have their punishments modified
articles.summary: Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina, and Thiago Almada have their punishments modified
articles.body:
The Argentine Football Association (AFA) announced that FIFA modified the sanction against its national team players for the incidents that occurred in the 2026 World Cup final against Spain , following a request for the suspended matches to be counted in friendlies and official Conmebol matches , according to a statement published this Thursday.

The Argentine Football Association sent a formal request to FIFA so that the sanctions imposed on its footballers during the 2026 World Cup final and on the association itself, can be served in Class "A" friendly matches and/or official matches , whichever comes first," explained the top football authority in the South American country, which added that the request " has been approved .

FIFA handed down a suspension of ten matches to Leandro Paredes, seven to Nahuel Molina, one to Thiago Almada and three to member of the coaching staff Roberto Ayala , over the incidents on the field after last July's final in which Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 .

In its statement this Thursday, the AFA stressed that it will persist with the appeal of the sanctions , which also included financial fines and crowd restrictions for home matches.

'“The Argentine Football Association, in defense of its rights and those of its footballers, is awaiting the grounds for the decisions in order to file the corresponding appeals before FIFA’s Appeals Committee, with CAS potentially as the final instance ,” the AFA statement concluded.'

'The AFA's legal advisor, Andrés Paton Urich , said last Friday in an interview with DSports radio: "We consider the sanctions to be excessive and will seek to have them reduced".'

The Argentine entity was punished with a fine of $321,000 pursuant to various articles of the FIFA Disciplinary Code for incidents in the team's matches against Cape Verde, Egypt, Switzerland, England and Spain during the World Cup, and it will also have to play its next two home matches with a spectator restriction (50%).
